known.via: English Wikipedia "Ancient Lakes of Columbia Valley AVA" (redirects to "Ancient Lakes of Columbia Valley")

climate: Seasons this mild ripen Chardonnay, Merlot, Syrah, Riesling and Sauvignon Blanc fully without cooking off their freshness.
Merlot, Syrah and Chardonnay sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.
Cabernet Sauvignon is at its cool limit. In cool years it can stay underripe, with green, sharp flavors.
Summers are close to rainless. Vines need irrigation or deep soil that stores winter rain, but disease is rare.

soil.rock: Volcanic rock is porous, so it drains well and sends roots deep. Lava soils are mostly basalt, rich in iron, calcium and magnesium. Sand is warm and airy. It drains fast but holds little water, and phylloxera does not thrive in it. Loess is fine, wind-blown silt. Fertile and warm, it holds water well but drains poorly.
soil.top: The topsoil drains well and still stores water for dry spells, so vines grow evenly. Its high pH can starve vines of iron and yellow the leaves, so growers plant lime-tolerant rootstocks.

land: Mostly flat. Easy and cheap to farm by machine, but on still nights cold air settles on flat ground, so spring frost is a bigger risk.
